Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be a brief pause while the system polls for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova Inc.'s Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; and Casey Wong, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of ShopNova Inc.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong third quarter performance, driven by robust active buyer growth and efficient marketing execution, alongside resilient operations amid macroeconomic pressures. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with gross merchandise value, or GMV, reaching $35 billion, up 22% year-over-year, and active buyers expanding to 152 million, an 18% increase.

Our focus remains on optimizing our marketplace dynamics through targeted fee structure adjustments that have encouraged seller expansion and higher-quality listings. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our enhanced AI-driven personalization tools, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates and average order values heading into the holidays.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience and holiday inventory positioning to meet anticipated demand surges.

We are focused on improving return on ad spend and customer lifetime value through data-centric marketing.

Finally, we are committed to navigating macroeconomic headwinds while capitalizing on emerging opportunities in high-growth regions like APAC.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our third quarter revenue was $1.8 billion, an increase of 28% year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 45%, driven by take-rate improvements from our marketplace fee optimizations and fulfillment efficiencies in our proprietary network. Operating expenses were $700 million, representing 39% of revenue. Our marketing investments remained disciplined, yielding strong returns as we'll discuss shortly.

Our net income for the quarter was $250 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue between $7.2 billion and $7.5 billion, with adjusted EBITDA margins of 18-20%.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive deeper into the marketing engine fueling this growth, I'd like to focus on one of our core KPIs: customer acquisition cost, or CAC, and the efficiency and ROI of our marketing spend. In e-commerce, where margins are tight and competition is fierce—from Amazon's dominance to Shopify-powered independents like Shein and Temu—mastering CAC is essential for sustainable scaling. We're acquiring customers profitably, with a sharp emphasis on lifetime value, or LTV, optimization.

The headline numbers: In Q3, our blended CAC was $45, a 13% improvement from $52 in Q3 last year and flat sequentially from Q1. This efficiency was achieved on $152 million in total marketing spend, which brought in 3.38 million new customers—our strongest cohort yet. By channel, paid social, mainly Meta Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns and TikTok Shop integrations, drove 42% of acquisitions at a $38 CPA; search via Google Performance Max and Bing Ads at $52 CPA for 28%; and emerging channels like connected TV and digital out-of-home at $65 CPA, but delivering 2.5 times higher LTV from premium audiences.

Our marketing ROI stands at an industry-leading 4.8 times ROAS—every dollar spent generated $4.80 in revenue within the first 12 months—up from 4.2 times year-over-year. This yields an LTV-to-CAC ratio of 6.7 to 1, based on a 24-month forward LTV of $302 per customer. For perspective, sector benchmarks from Profitero and peers like Wayfair at 4-5 times ROAS or Etsy's $60-70 CAC average 3-4 to 1, so we're ahead thanks to our proprietary first-party data and proactive moves against third-party cookie deprecation ahead of Google's phase-out.

Trends show CAC stabilizing after the 2022-2023 inflation surge, where industry averages rose 20-30% from iOS privacy shifts and CPM hikes. Our year-over-year deleveraging comes from a 22% rise in organic traffic to 35% of visits, powered by SEO in sustainable fashion and smart home tech, plus Pinterest and Reddit syndication. Paid gains include a 17% Facebook CPM drop via dynamic creative optimization and a 25% uplift from YouTube Shorts incrementality tests showing 15% true lift.

Regionally, across our 15 markets—45% North America revenue, 30% EMEA, 25% APAC: North America CAC at $40 benefits from mature infrastructure and loyalty tiers lifting LTV 18%, with payback under four months as we gain electronics share. EMEA at $55 reflects GDPR retargeting limits, but localized influencers delivered 8 times ROAS and 10% year-over-year clawback. APAC at $35 leverages super-app ties like Shopee, though higher churn prompts gamified onboarding improving Day-30 retention 12 points and effective CAC 15%.

On the tech side, our in-house ML bidding engine on TensorFlow and Snowflake handles multi-touch attribution, allocating 65% to upper-funnel while proving incrementality. Post-privacy updates, server-side tracking on Shopify Plus and BigQuery recovers 85% signal, with Google's Conversions API boosting search ROAS 22%. Generative AI creatives cut costs 40% and lift CTR 15% via personalized variants.

Strategically, we're shifting 20% of budget to performance max and affiliates like Rakuten for 5 times ROAS floors, prioritizing cohort quality—loyalty referrals yield 3 times LTV at zero CAC. Q4 CAC should dip to $43 with holiday ramps, full-year at $44-46, backed by $50 million marketing tech R&D.

Building on this marketing discipline, let's turn to advertising and marketing spend efficiency, spotlighting return on ad spend, or ROAS—revenue per ad dollar via ad-attributed revenue over spend. It's our guidepost for profitable scale amid 12-15% industry CAC rises from consumer softness and ATT changes.

Q3 blended ROAS hit 5.2 times, up 8% year-over-year from 4.8 times and sequentially from 5.0 times, on $285 million spend—17.2% of GMV, down 120 basis points year-over-year. This beats 3.5-4.0 times peer benchmarks amid Google and Meta auction pressures.

By channel: Search and Performance Max at 7.1 times ROAS, 42% of ad revenue, holding prospecting at 4.5 times despite 10% CPC hikes via ML intent prediction from 150 million loyalty members—Performance Max now 60% of search. Social commerce at 4.8 times, up from 4.2 times, with Meta retargeting at 5.5 times and TikTok at 6.2 times on beauty UGC. Retail media and Amazon DSP at 4.1 times, our ShopNova Media Network hitting 8 times internally with P&G partners. Emerging programmatic at 3.9 times, Reddit niche ads at 5.5 times.

Regions: North America 5.6 times on Prime Day tails; EMEA 4.5 times against GDPR dips, targeting 5.0 times H2; APAC 4.9 times led by India Flipkart ties.

Drivers: NovaBid Pro AI bidding lifted 15%; Bayesian attribution uncovered 32% upper-funnel revenue; shifts to loyalty at 9.2 times ROAS and micro-influencers at 6.8 times. Q4 guide 5.3-5.5 times, resilient via 40/30/30 channel split and Unified ID 2.0.

Underpinning these efficiencies is active buyer count growth, defining actives as trailing 12-month purchasers aligning with Amazon and Alibaba standards.

Q3 globals reached 152 million actives, 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter growth, beating guidance. Trailing GMV $28.5 billion up 22%, ARPU $187 up 3%.

Acquisition added 28 million net trailing, 7.2 million Q3 at $42 CAC—paid at 3.2 times ROAS via TikTok and CTV; organic 32% from SEO and influencers generating 12 million zero-CAC sign-ups; Nova Prime upgrades 2.5 million at 65% trial conversion. NovaAI boosts first-purchase 22%, AR try-ons 3 times Gen Z conversions. LTV:CAC 4.1 to 1 despite U.S. moderation.

Retention at 68% 12-month cohorts, up 400 bps, 4.2 orders/year, 2.1% monthly churn. Nova Prime 52% penetration, 2.5 times retention; BOPIS up 35%; BNPL 28% carts cut churn 15%. Regions: NA 84 million, 70% retention; EMEA 30 million; APAC/LATAM 38 million at 75%.

AI lifecycle and Green Cart lift loyalty; FY24 capex $450 million targets 20% growth, Q4 4-6% sequential.

Shifting to marketplace dynamics, our recent fee structure updates—rolled early July in electronics, apparel, home & garden (65% GMV)—tiered referrals 12-18% by performance and fulfillment, FBN discounts, ad uplifts over 20% ACoS, volume rebates over $1 million GMV.

Active sellers hit 2.8 million, up 7% sequential; high-volume expanded listings 22%, adding 15 million SKUs. Low-volume churn 3% offset by onboarding AI. GMV/seller $10,200 up 11%, ad take-rate 32%. Nexus AI cut ACoS 18% to 24%, Sponsored Products budget +25%, units +14%. FBN 62% units, delivery 97% two-day.

Regions: NA 94% retention, +28% assortment; APAC offset 5% churn with inflows; Europe pivoted via VAT tools. Flywheel lifts take-rate 22.4%, seller profitability +6%, AOV +4% to $48. FY24 $150 million Nexus expansion for 200-300 bps EBITDA.

Even amid these strengths, macroeconomic factors impacted GMV and revenue. Q3 GMV $35 billion up 22%, but macros dragged 2-3 points; revenue $1.8 billion up 28% via 22.1% take-rate and ad surge.

Inflation at 4.2% shrank AOV 4% to $52, baskets 7%, fashion/electronics soft; essentials buffered. Rates crimped durables 6%; supply/geopolitics cut SKUs 3%, cross-border -2%. NA 5% U.S. growth on events; Europe flat; APAC/LATAM +22-30%.

Countered with GenAI pricing +15% conversions, nearshoring -25% lead times, Value Vault +12% traffic, Prime churn 4%.

Q4 GMV 9-11% implied.

Finally, holiday prep: Inventory $2.8 billion up 18%, AI-sensed for $1.2 trillion spend. Electronics $850 million +22%, apparel $650 million, home/beauty $1.1 billion. Sourcing diversified, lead times 45 days, 28 centers.

Q4 GMV $18-20 billion, 24-30% growth, 450 million orders at $145 AOV. BFCM $4.5 billion, category shifts, Elite 55% volume. ML orchestration 92% accurate, GenAI 12% AOV; coverage 105-110%.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment scalability and seller integration post-fee updates, alongside supply chain diversification. Our shipping times improved by 25% to under two days for 97% of Prime-eligible orders. Fulfillment costs declined 15% through FBN adoption and robotics in new centers. We are implementing advanced warehouse management systems with dynamic slotting to handle holiday peaks without stockouts.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Advantage+ campaigns and TikTok Shop integrations, alongside micro-influencer expansions. Customer acquisition costs held at $45 with 4.8 times ROAS overall. Our brand awareness increased by 20% per NPS surveys. We are focusing on privacy-first incrementality testing and GenAI creatives to sustain efficiency into Q4.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Wong.

Casey Wong:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on ML bidding engines like NovaBid Pro and server-side attribution to combat signal loss. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%, driven by AR try-ons and personalized feeds. We're investing in generative AI for recommendations and inventory forecasting to power holiday demand sensing.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions: Press star one for questions. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Thanks. Jordan, great detail on CAC and ROAS—impressive efficiencies. Can you expand on how you're planning to maintain LTV:CAC above 6:1 amid holiday subsidy pressures from Temu?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, our focus on cohort quality over volume is key. Loyalty referrals at zero CAC and 3 times LTV, combined with AI personalization lifting repeat rates, keeps us at 6.7:1. Holiday ramps will test this, but with ROAS floors at 5 times and upper-funnel allocation, we're confident.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Torres with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Torres:
Hi team. On macros, how are you seeing consumer sentiment evolve into holidays, especially durables?

Alex Rivera:
Lisa, sentiment remains cautious per Nielsen at 62% trading down, but our value tiers and private label up 25% position us well. Events like BFCM should drive 25% GMV lift, with essentials and gifting resilient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Taylor, on ops—fulfillment costs down 15%, but with inventory up 18%, any margin risks in Q4?

Taylor Kim:
Great question, Raj. No risks—our ML orchestration at 92% accuracy minimizes stockouts and overstock, with nearshoring cutting costs further. FBN at 62% units ensures 18% EBITDA delivery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Grant with Barclays.

Emily Grant:
Riley, marketing spend efficiency shines. Thoughts on emerging channels like CTV contributing to 20% brand awareness gain?

Riley Patel:
Emily, CTV and DOOH are high-LTV plays at 2.5 times despite $65 CPA. Incrementality tests show strong lift, and with Reddit at 5.5 times ROAS, we're allocating more for Q4 awareness.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Citi.

David Kim:
Casey, impressive tech stack. How is Nexus AI impacting seller ACoS post-fee changes?

Casey Wong:
David, Nexus AI on 500 petabytes reduced ACoS 18% to 24%, boosting Sponsored Products 14%. Globally expanding with elasticity models for 10-15% seller LTV uplift.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
